capture_source: live capture 2026-08-26 at the transport seam; SAP A4H kernel 793 release 758, sysnr 00, gateway port 3300, unicode, codepage 4103
evidence: recorded by wrapping Transport.recv_message around a single Connection.ping(); return code 0x0420 == 0, ping() returned True
notes: Captured ABOVE the NI layer — no 4-byte NI length prefix; the frame starts at the GW header.
The server-direction RFC marker at [76:80] is 00000002, NOT the client-direction ffff0004. The 80-byte strip is driven by the leading 0x06 GW-frame byte, so it is unaffected by the marker value.
The GW header carries the negotiated codepage as ASCII '4103' at offset 69.

Regression guard for issue #7: the return code 0x0420 is the FOURTH record, not the first. Preceded by 0x0500, 0x0503 and a 16-byte 0x0514 session token, each followed by a repeated close tag. A reader that does not skip the close tag desynchronises by two bytes before reaching 0x0420; one that does not strip the GW header reads gw_version (0x0200 = 512) as a TLV length, which is the 'length 512 exceeds remaining payload' signature reported in issue #7.

Sanitised, byte length preserved: the GW conversation handle at [40:48] replaced with '00000000', and the 16-byte 0x0514 session token value at [96:112] replaced with bytes 0x00..0x0f. Nothing else altered; no credentials or hostnames present.

Tag 0x0667 is an 8-byte little-endian IEEE-754 double, 138.0 in this capture. The bytes are confirmed; the meaning is NOT. This note previously asserted 'call duration in microseconds', which a capture cannot establish. A live probe has since disproven the timeout reading -- the value moved 400x across three calls -- but has not separated 'microseconds of server time' from 'bytes of response', because both grow with the rows read. See docs/protocol/framing.md. Requests carry the 8-byte invoke footer in the same position; responses carry this instead.

field_annotations.note: server-side call duration: IEEE-754 double, LITTLE-endian, in microseconds. This capture decodes to 138.0 us; big-endian yields a denormal (2.08e-317), so the byte order is unambiguous. Note the TLV tag and length are BIG-endian while this payload is little-endian - byte order is per-field, not per-connection.
